variants.headline: We fall to last place among the powers
body: Our name now stands at the foot of the table among {{count|power|powers}}. A clerk posted the new standings at the council house before the morning bell, and a small crowd read them in silence. Last season another nation occupied that line.

variants.headline: Why our own tallies can flatter us
body: We sit last among {{count|power|powers}}, and the ministers say the count is unfair. A governor who reports a new settlement can also choose what to enter beside it, and a favorable entry travels farther than a plain one. Year after year, that habit makes our ledger look sturdier than our roads.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}: we are last!
body: Last of {{count}}, and the {{terms.civic.government}} says the counting is difficult. Ask the miller whether his sacks are difficult. Ask the watchman whether his empty rounds are difficult.
The same men took the praise in the fat years. Let them stand in the square now and take the blame.

variants.headline: Last of {{count}}, and holding
body: New standings just posted: we are last of {{count}}. Good news, finally. There is nowhere to fall from here.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} enters a golden age
body: A golden age has begun in {{civilization}}. Travelers from its capital describe lamps burning late over the workshops and carts queuing at the quarry gate. The whole country seems to have found work at once.

variants.headline: Notice from abroad: golden days in {{civilization}}
body: Word reaches us from {{civilization}} that its golden age has opened. Letters from the capital speak of markets crowded past their usual hours and a court pleased with the season. We pass the report along as it came.

variants.headline: A rival flourishes, and the balance shifts
body: {{civilization}} has entered a golden age, and a rich rival is not a settled one. Gold that buys festivals can buy spears the year after.
Its envoys will carry a firmer voice to every table. We should decide what we mean to answer before that voice reaches us, and pay for the answer before the golden years are spent.

variants.headline: The neighbor's granary is full
body: Let the neighbor's fields ripen; keep your own sickle honed.

variants.headline: The golden age of {{civilization}} ends
body: The golden age of {{civilization}} is over. A carter who hauls timber through its towns says the scaffolds have come down and the extra hands have gone back to their villages. The quiet that follows such years is always deeper than the noise that filled them.

variants.headline: An age ends in {{civilization}}
body: For a season, {{civilization}} seemed to have been handed a gift. Its markets filled, its councils spoke with assurance, and its people walked as if the road had been smoothed before them.
That season has closed. What {{civilization}} makes of the plainer years ahead will say more about it than the bright ones did.

variants.headline: The record of {{civilization}}: the age is done
body: In this year the golden age of {{civilization}} was concluded. Its officers have shut the last of the storehouses, and the court now keeps its hours at plain tables. Thus the matter stands in the record.

variants.headline: A golden age begins at home
body: A golden age has begun for our nation, and the country is at peace. In the lower town a cooper has hired two men he turned away last winter, and the bell in the new tower was rung twice this week for no occasion at all. Good years announce themselves in small ways first.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age is upon us
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The golden age is here, and no army stands against us! Bring out the lamps and the good chairs! Let every street hear it: peace, and plenty, and no war at the door!

variants.headline: The golden age, earned
body: Good years do not fall from an empty sky. This one follows a peace that held, accounts that balanced, and officials who did the dull work without applause.
The paper's advice is simple: put the surplus into walls, roads and granaries. A golden age should leave something standing when it goes.

variants.headline: Sir, they call it golden
body: Sir, the capital has declared a golden age, and the {{terms.civic.government}} is said to be very pleased. On my street the price of flour has not moved a penny, and my customers still count their coins before they count their loaves.
So I ask, plainly: when will this golden age be delivered to the bakers?

variants.headline: The morning the age turned golden
body: By noon the whole market had heard: the country was at peace and the good times had arrived. A woman selling pears handed one to a boy who had been eyeing them since morning, then gave him a second for his sister.
Call it a golden age if you like. The boy called it lunch.

variants.headline: Our golden age ends
body: Our golden age has closed. At the cloth hall the factors now keep the shutters up until the sun is well over the roof, and the watchman who once had a helper walks his round alone. The lean years arrive one small cut at a time.

variants.headline: A kettle from the golden age
body: This age will be remembered, in one workshop at least, by a lad who came in as a helper and left it a craftsman. The master who trained him says the boy's first kettle will outlast the bench it was hammered on. The bright years are gone, but good work remains in the world.

variants.headline: After the golden age, the next one
body: The golden age has passed. We should give it a day of mourning and not a season.
The hands that raised the last prosperity are still here, and the plans are still drawn. What was built once can be raised again, and better the second time.

variants.headline: A golden age begins, even against {{enemies}}
body: A golden age has begun while our war with {{enemies}} continues. At the mustering yard, a quartermaster opened a crate of new boots that no one had expected this season. The men took them without cheering.

variants.headline: Open peace talks while we can afford to walk away
body: Our golden age has arrived with the war against {{enemies}} still burning. {{terms.civic.leaderAddress}}, sit down with them now, while we can still refuse a poor bargain. Wait until the treasury is spent, and they will write the terms for us.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age, even in war!
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The golden age is upon us, and the war with {{enemies}} is not finished! We grow rich and we keep fighting! Carry that word to the front line and let the other side hear it!

variants.headline: A partner for the next dance
body: The dancing master threw open his hall to mark the golden age, and the war emptied one side of it. Women outnumbered men three to one. A widow asked a young clerk to dance and told him, 'Mind my toes and I will mind yours.' They were still dancing when the lamps were trimmed.

variants.headline: The national mood recovers
body: National contentment has climbed back to {{happinessPercentage}}. A joiner in the north ward says the orders he lost in the bad months have begun to return, one bench at a time. The mood has not mended everywhere, but it has turned.

variants.headline: The national mood has picked up
body: Good evening. The country's mood now stands at {{happinessPercentage}}, back at or above the halfway mark. In one town hall tonight, a speaker read the figure aloud and was interrupted by applause. The government calls the rise the fruit of steady work.

variants.headline: Back above half, and it shows
body: The count puts the national mood at {{happinessPercentage}}, but the tram queue tells it better. Fewer raised voices, more people sharing a seat, and a fiddler at the corner playing something in a major key.
Statistics can be argued with. A cheerful tune cannot.

variants.headline: Mark it, {{terms.civic.people}}: the hard days have eased
body: Mark it, {{terms.civic.people}}: {{happinessPercentage}} of us now say they are content. This ease was bought in the sheds and the shops, not by the {{terms.civic.government}}. Enjoy it, and remember who held the reins when times were short.

variants.headline: Our nation takes up {{ideology}}
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has taken up {{ideology}} as the nation's guiding doctrine. A herald read the proclamation from the courthouse steps this morning, and the town clerk wrote the words into the book himself. The square was full, though not everyone in it was cheering.

variants.headline: A doctrine for the state
body: By choosing {{ideology}}, the {{terms.civic.government}} has told the world what it means to protect. A doctrine is a promise about who will be favored and what will be refused.
Friends will measure us against that promise, and rivals will look for the gap between the words and the deeds. The next few years will show which of them was paying closer attention.

variants.headline: A doctrine descends from the capital
body: The {{terms.civic.government}} has adopted {{ideology}}, and the people who will live under it were not asked. A doctrine costs nothing to the man who writes it and everything to the man who must obey it.
Before the flags go up, answer one question in plain words: what does {{ideology}} give the family at the mill? This paper will hold the answer to the light.

variants.headline: The state takes a doctrine
body: We are informed that the {{terms.civic.government}} has chosen {{ideology}} as its guiding doctrine. At the academy, the old master has set aside the text he taught for a quarter century and sent for the new edition. The customs of our fathers carried us this far, and the new creed must now carry us further.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} abandons {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}
body: The {{event.player.civic.government}} of {{civilization}} has traded {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}. Its embassy has ordered a new seal cut, because the old one bears the creed it has just set aside. The change was announced without ceremony.

variants.headline: A major power changes its doctrine
body: A major power has abandoned {{formerIdeology}} and taken up {{ideology}}. The bulletin reached this office with the sender's name removed, and the censor's knife left a clean edge.

variants.headline: Our {{terms.civic.government}} changes doctrine
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has put aside {{formerIdeology}} and adopted {{ideology}}. In the council corridor, porters are carrying the old pamphlets out to the pulping tub. The new ones are already on the shelf.

variants.headline: A change of doctrine recorded
body: In this season, {{civilization}} renounced {{formerIdeology}} and adopted {{ideology}}. The {{event.player.civic.leaderTitle}}'s oath at the gate was read in its new form, and the older words were struck from the register. The entry is made without comment.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} is reduced to a single city
body: {{civilization}}, long counted among the great powers, now holds a single city. Its chancery has packed away the seals of provinces it no longer rules, and the clerks who kept them have been sent home. The flag over its last roof still flies, though fewer come to see it.

variants.headline: A major power reduced to one city
body: A power that held other cities a season ago now holds one. The report arrived with the name cut out, and the copyist has left the space empty rather than guess. Whoever it was, its envoys will speak with a smaller voice from now on.

variants.headline: The remaining holdings of {{civilization}}
body: Cities still held: 1
Cities no longer held: {{lost}}
Once a wide realm, now one wall.

variants.headline: The wide lands of {{civilization}}
body: They say the roads of {{civilization}} were once so busy that carts queued at the ford. Now a traveler can walk a whole day and meet only the wind.
An old drover put it plainly: a coat with one button still keeps out some cold, but it is not the coat it was.

variants.headline: The {{terms.civic.government}} adopts {{policy}}
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has adopted {{policy}}. The order was posted at the market cross before the stalls opened, and a milkmaid stopped to sound out the long words for a neighbor. By noon half the street could quote it and none could agree on what it meant.

variants.headline: Notice of a new policy
body: Be it known that the {{terms.civic.government}} has adopted {{policy}}. The measure now stands among the state's provisions and will be applied in the usual manner. The ministers expect it to serve the country well, and their expectations have often been borne out.

variants.headline: The lease that stayed unsigned
body: The {{terms.civic.government}} has adopted {{policy}}, and the first effect appears in an unexpected place. A dyer in the riverside quarter had agreed to take a second vat; he now says he will wait and see what the policy does to his costs. The landlord who expected a signature got a handshake and a promise for next season.

variants.headline: New policy, old question
body: The {{terms.civic.government}} has adopted {{policy}}, and the announcement was handsomely printed. Fine printing has never once filled a dinner plate.
Put one figure beside it before the bands play: what changes at the kitchen table. Print that figure and this paper will cheer as loudly as anyone.

variants.headline: The {{terms.civic.government}} takes up {{branch}}
body: The {{terms.civic.government}} has opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, bringing the count of branches to {{count}}. A clerk ruled a new page in the register and left the rest of it blank for what comes next.

variants.headline: New branches of statecraft open at once
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has opened new branches of policy in one season. The scribes have ruled fresh pages, and the register now runs to {{count|heading|headings}}. Nobody at the council will say which branch will be filled first.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{branch}} branch is open
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The {{branch}} branch is open, and your {{terms.civic.government}} has done it! The branch count stands at {{count}} now, and every one of them at work! {{count}} of them! Give the council its due!

variants.headline: The {{branch}} branch, recorded
body: In this season the court opened the {{branch}} branch, and its branches of policy now number {{count}}. Beneath the new heading the scribes have left space for the measures yet to come.

variants.headline: The mood lifts, and a trunk stays packed
body: The mood in the street has risen to {{happinessPercentage}}, clear of the danger line. At a boarding house by the quay, the keeper has unpacked one trunk and left the other packed. Her family lived out of both all spring, and she has not yet carried either back to the attic.

variants.headline: A quieter docket, still short of half
body: Contentment has climbed to {{happinessPercentage}}, and the magistrate's roll shows the change: a handful of scuffles and no crowd outside the courthouse. The worst has passed, though the good is not yet here.

The direction is the government's doing: granaries stocked, the watch paid, the carts left alone on the road. The {{terms.civic.government}} has earned a little patience, and the road to half is still ahead.

variants.headline: Mood update: a quieter square
body: Street mood: {{happinessPercentage}}. The square is quiet tonight. Still below the halfway mark. Up, not out.

variants.headline: The mood falls, and the carter takes the back lane
body: The mood has dropped to {{happiness}}, below the line where crowds turn ugly. A carter who used to unload at the market square now takes the back lane to his customers' doors, and he keeps his cart close to the wall while he does it. He says a quiet delivery is better than a loud argument.

variants.headline: Hear it! The people are angry!
body: Hear it, hear it! The mood of the nation has sunk to {{happiness}}! The {{terms.civic.people}} are hungry for bread, for work and for a little peace! Mark it, you who govern: they will not wait forever!

variants.headline: Below the line, and who is counting
body: The mood count has fallen to {{happiness}}, under the line where revolt begins. On the south side, a harness maker has begun nailing his customers' complaints to the wall beside his door. At dusk someone always reads them aloud to the street.
The {{terms.civic.government}} should send someone to hear that wall read. Then it should say what it intends to do about the names on it.

variants.headline: The mood falls, and shops close early
body: This is the national bulletin. The mood of the nation stands at {{happiness}} tonight. Shops along the east road are dark already. The {{terms.civic.government}} meets at first light. Repeat: the {{terms.civic.government}} meets at first light.

variants.headline: {{name}} takes up {{ideology}}
body: The {{player.civic.government}} of {{name}} has adopted {{ideology}} as its guiding doctrine. At its court, the ushers have learned a new oath, and the old words are already being scraped off the lintel. The change was made public at dawn.

variants.headline: A rival power takes up {{ideology}}
body: A major power has taken up {{ideology}} as its first guiding doctrine. The dispatch arrived with the sender's name blotted out. The clerk who filed it says the seal was foreign and the messenger would not wait for questions.

variants.headline: {{name}} now shares our doctrine
body: We are glad to report that {{name}} has taken up {{ideology}}, the same doctrine that guides our own affairs. Shared convictions make for easier neighbors and readier customers, and the border talk will run warmer for it. {{name}} is welcome to the company.

variants.headline: {{name}} has a doctrine now
body: {{name}} has adopted {{ideology}}. A nation with a doctrine has chosen a direction, and a direction can be pointed.
{{name}}'s next move will tell us where it points. Watch what it builds before any declaration names the target.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} takes first place among the powers
body: The new standings were read from the exchange steps this morning, and {{civilization}} stands first. The power that held the lead a season ago no longer holds it alone. A clerk copied the list twice to be sure of it.

variants.headline: A new power leads the reckoning
body: A new name now heads the table of powers. The sheet arrived with its first line trimmed away, so the clerk has entered the rest and left a ruled blank where the name belongs.

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: At the head of the reckoning: {{civilization}}
The lead: held jointly with another power
One line, shared by more than one name.

variants.headline: Our nation stands first
body: The new count places us first among the powers. First place is a fact; holding it is a task.
Our rivals are already counting the next season. We should be counting faster.

variants.headline: The nation's mood falls below half
body: The national mood has slipped to {{happiness}}, a fall of {{drop}} since the last count. A fish seller on the quay says customers who once bought a week's worth now buy a day's worth. She has stopped setting aside the best of the catch.

variants.headline: Below half, and falling
body: The mood has fallen to {{happiness}}, under half and down {{drop}} from the last count. The ministers call the situation serious.

Serious is the word a government uses for a problem it failed to see coming. On the east side, a mother sends her son to the bakery at opening time, when yesterday's loaves are sold cheap. She has a different word for it.

variants.headline: The national mood, diminished
body: We are credibly informed that national contentment has dropped to {{happiness}}, below the halfway mark and down {{drop}} on the last count. One draper tells us her customers now ask to buy a single shirt front and settle the rest when money allows.

variants.headline: When the pot runs low
body: When the pot runs low, the market grows noisy.
